sections.content:
Population change in Selby in 2032

The population in Selby is projected to increase from 93,613 people in 2022 to 104,720 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 10,311 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Selby
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Selby, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • Births and deaths is not projected to change the population substantially, with 9,399 births and 9,455 deaths in Selby between 2022 and 2032. There will be an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 10,311, with 60,304 people moving to the area and 49,993 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Selby by 11.0%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is not projected to change the population substantially, with 1,194 people moving to the area and 1,249 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 791, with 2,426 people moving to the area and 1,636 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Selby by 0.8%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Selby in 2032

The median age in Selby is projected to rise from 43 years in 2022 to 44 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 23% of the population in Selby are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 19% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Selby between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Selby is projected to stay the same, at around 61%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 310 to 342 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Selby?

In 2032, 20% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 21% in 2022.

This is the same as the average for England in 2032.

Looking at the youngest age groups in Selby between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
